bullets.title: Fed Chair Warsh signals hawkish pivot; Sept hike odds jump to ~58-60%
bullets.body: Warsh's Jackson Hole speech was the dominant macro event of the period, reiterating the Fed's commitment to returning PCE to 2% and warning inflation isn't slowing meaningfully. September hike odds repriced from ~35-36% to ~57-60% (CME/Kalshi); Barclays shifted to forecasting two 25bp hikes (Sept + Dec). The 2-year Treasury yield jumped ~12bps to ~4.35%, bear-flattening the curve. Fedlock analysis notes Warsh is still the most dovish FOMC member relative to his colleagues even in absolute hawkish tones—actual vote expected 7-5.

bullets.title: Oil surges 3-4% on US-Iran military exchange; Strait of Hormuz disruption risk elevated
bullets.body: US forces struck Iranian rocket launchers on Larak Island; Iran retaliated with ballistic missile strikes on US bases in Jordan (intercepted with no significant damage) and drone strikes, while claiming to have downed a US MQ-9. WTI reached ~$84-87 and Brent touched above $90. A tanker was struck by mines/projectile near Hormuz; shipping through the strait fell to ~5 vessels daily over the weekend. Saudi Arabia reportedly in talks to raise $8B in loans. European natural gas futures rose ~5%.

bullets.title: Macro tape: strong US corporate profits, sticky inflation, hawkish rates but solid growth
bullets.body: Nancy Lazar (PSC) flags nominal GDP at 6.6% y/y with fed funds at 3.6% (300bp stimulative gap), 2Q corporate revenue growth of 8.3% y/y, and 10 signs of sticky inflation including core goods, super-core services, and accelerating M2/bank loans. GDP price deflator hit 4.4% y/y and 6.4% q/q annualized in 2Q. Consumer sentiment (UM) at 51.7, down ~6% MoM; discounters outperforming. Student loan SAVE reset puts $9.7B of annual consumer spending at risk.

bullets.title: JPM shifts tactically cautious/neutral; favors Mag7 over Semis, expects choppy 3-4 weeks
bullets.body: JPM notes September is historically the worst month for SPX, Fed now priced at 60% hike, positioning at 37th percentile, and credit spreads likely to widen post-Labor Day issuance spike. Corporate profits up 41% QoQ (5-year best). Momentum indices down 21-34% from June highs. Recommends reducing net longs, favoring Mag7 over Semis, and using IWM options for FOMC/economic data trades. SPX risk range cited at 7,625-7,749.

bullets.title: Sector rotation: Software/IGV +20% QTD, Semis/SOX -20%; 'SaaSaissance' vs semis bear market
bullets.body: H1:26 saw semis outperform and software underperform; Q3:26 reversed sharply. SOX briefly entered bear market before finding 100-day MA support. CRM jumped +22.4% in 5 days (largest move since 2020) post-earnings. IGV outperformed +5.9% in the week. Memory stocks up 29% avg in August after -47% in July. Citi TMT Conference (Sept 8-10) shows top requested meetings shifted to 80% semis/hardware vs. 50/50 prior year, creating potential software discovery opportunity.

bullets.title: Global rates moving higher: German Bunds at 15-year high, JGBs hitting multi-decade peaks
bullets.body: Germany's 10-year Bund yield hit 3.29% (15-year high); 2-year Bund at 2.90% (highest since July 2024). Japan's 2-year JGB surged to 1.73-1.75% (31-year high), 10-year to 2.95%, and 30-year to 4.145%. Japan spent a record ¥15.4 trillion (≈$96.4B) in July-August supporting the yen, which nevertheless slipped back through 160/USD. Treasury Secretary Bessent described yen moves as 'pretty contained.' South Korea hiked 25bps to 3.00% for a second consecutive month.

bullets.title: Trump-Venezuela oil deal: US to take majority control of 65B+ barrels; strategic reserve implications
bullets.body: Trump announced what he called the 'biggest oil deal in world history'—the US will take majority control (~55%) of output from a JV covering 65+ billion barrels of Venezuelan proven reserves. Venezuela targets 1.5M bpd production. Deal faces practical challenges including aging infrastructure, heavy sour crude incompatibility with SPR salt-cavern storage, and political opposition on both sides. Iran sanctions concurrently tightened; US Saudi crude imports dropped to zero for first time since 1985.

bullets.title: AI capex: Hyperscaler backlog surges 151% YoY to $1.7T; global AI capex to reach $3.8T by 2030
bullets.body: Citi TMT Conference preview highlights hyperscaler CROCI consistently ~30% supporting the AI ecosystem. NVDA guided FY28 revenue at ~$700B (70% YoY growth vs. consensus 43%), projecting $1.3T of hyperscaler capex in 2027 (up 63% YoY). Warsh's Jackson Hole speech noted AI-related capex drove ~50% of recent investment growth. Tech capex deflator up 7.3% y/y in 2Q signals supply/demand imbalance. Power infrastructure is the 2027 bottleneck: ~15GW of AI compute expected to be produced but undeployable due to transformer, cooling, and networking constraints.

bullets.title: Memory market tightening severely into 2027; DRAM ASPs seen +44% YoY; PC/smartphone BOM shock
bullets.body: UBS projects DRAM fulfillment rate at ~60%; server DDR bit demand growth pushing ~80% YoY in 2027. DRAM sufficiency ratio forecast at -6% to -12% in 2027 vs. -8% in 2026E. DRAM blended ASPs forecast +44% YoY in 2027 (after +240% in 2026E), suppressed by LTA pricing. HBM demand forecast at 61.5Bn Gb in 2027 (+91% YoY). PC DRAM/NAND combos up 340% YoY in non-flagship phones. TrendForce raised Q3 PC DRAM price forecast to +18-23% QoQ. SK Hynix reportedly weighing Intel Foundry for HBM4E base dies.

bullets.title: Hot Chips 2026: NVDA shifts to full-stack 100MW AI factories; ASICs settle at ~30% of market
bullets.body: NVDA's Rubin claims 10-30x higher token throughput per MW vs. Blackwell via NVFP4 sparsity and NVLink 6. AMD MI455X combines N2/N3P chiplets with 432GB HBM4/23.3TB/s; emphasizes open Ethernet/ESUN fabric. OpenAI Jalapeño ASIC (built by AVGO in 9 months) runs ~700W vs. ~1.2kW for GB200. Memory bandwidth now primary bottleneck—KV-cache growth driving architectural shifts. ASICs expected to stabilize at ~30% of accelerator market vs. 70% GPUs due to flexibility/ecosystem advantages.

bullets.title: NVDA acquires Hugging Face for $12.9B to build end-to-end AI platform
bullets.body: UBS SemiBytes reports NVDA is acquiring Hugging Face for $12.9B to expand its AI software stack beyond hardware into model layer, developer tools, and data. Strategy aims to build end-to-end AI platform spanning developers, data, models, and deployment. In-house open-source models should drive ecosystem adoption and inference demand. Separately, BofA sees NVDA 34-50% undervalued with $350 PT, with primary discount driven by OpenAI concentration risk (NVDA backstops $105B of residual value on OpenAI data centers).

bullets.title: US Housing: significant deterioration continuing—new home sales -6.3% YoY, price cuts at 97th percentile
bullets.body: Weekly housing tracker shows purchase applications fell to -3.3% YoY, pending sales at -3.1% YoY. New home sales dropped to 607K (-6.3% YoY). Single-family starts fell to 808K (-15.7% YoY). New-home months' supply at 9.6, price cuts at 20.8% of listings (97th percentile), cancellations at 14.7% (92nd percentile). 30-year mortgage stable at 6.66%. Nearly 1 in 5 outstanding US mortgages now carry rates above 6%.

bullets.title: Key earnings week: DELL, MDB, AVGO (Wed), HPE, CIEN, SNOW with high buyside bars
bullets.body: AVGO reports Sept 2 with buyside expecting >36% QoQ revenue growth, FY27 AI guide raise to $120B+ (some pushing $130B), and 2H26 supported by TPU v8i ramp and sold-out Tomahawk 6. JPM's Harlan Sur maintains $580 TP. Jefferies previews SNOW with 36% y/y product revenue expected vs. 30% guide; MDB with Atlas ~30.5-31% y/y vs. 26% guide. PANW FQ4 NGS ARR ~$840M vs. $795M guide. DELL EPS estimate 4.91, revenue 44.93B.

bullets.title: S&P 500 futures +0.2%; pre-market: energy leading, SaaS/cloud mixed, PINS -3% on CFO exit
bullets.body: S&P 500 futures at +0.23% to 7,704.5 pre-market Monday; WTI crude +3.38% to $86.22 on Iran tensions; 10-year yield stable at 4.72%. Energy broadly up 1-6% pre-market. Tech/SaaS mixed: TTD +3.9%, SNAP +3.1%; PINS -3.1% on CFO departure; Adobe -1.1%, Salesforce -1.2%, ServiceNow -2.8%. Europe modestly lower; Asian equities fell 0.8% (KOSPI -3%) on hawkish Fed signals and geopolitical risk. SHEIN gray market shares fell 11% in Hong Kong.

bullets.title: Apple CEO transition: John Ternus takes over Monday; Tim Cook moves to chairman role
bullets.body: Tim Cook's last day as Apple CEO is Monday August 31; John Ternus officially succeeds. Apple grew from $350B to ~$4.7T market cap under Cook (+25.6% avg annual return over 15 years). Ternus reportedly prioritizing AI with ambitious device slate including foldable iPhone and smart displays. Separately, Apple TV+ raised prices to $14.99/month (4th increase in 4 years; tripled from $4.99 launch). OpenAI and Anthropic reportedly using tens of thousands of Mac Minis for AI reinforcement learning workloads.

bullets.title: META $18B teen safety settlement removes litigation overhang; new AI products pending
bullets.body: META settled with 52 AGs paying up to $18B over 10 years with product restrictions (daily time limits, night mode for teens). META will accrue ~$10B legal charge in 3Q26 not in expense guidance. Revenue from teens is <1% of META total. Morgan Stanley draws analogy to GOOGL's post-DOJ 40% multiple expansion, arguing settlement could be a 'clearing event' for META. Settlement includes contingency payments encouraging YouTube/TikTok/Snap to adopt similar standards. Forward PE at ~17.9x, ~25% below long-term average.

bullets.title: China PMI: August manufacturing at 49.8 (beat), composite 49.5—still contracting; global asset managers exiting
bullets.body: China Manufacturing PMI: 49.8 vs. 49.5 est. (from 49.2 prior), slight sequential improvement but still below 50. Non-Manufacturing PMI: 49.0, below 49.4 estimate and unchanged. JPM flags 76% of China consumer coverage saw consensus cuts YTD; FY27 consensus embeds both demand recovery and margin expansion simultaneously—likely too optimistic. Global asset managers ('Chexit') reducing China exposure. South Korea KOSPI fell 3%+ on hawkish Fed signals.

bullets.title: VIX near 14-month lows; options market skew shifting post-Warsh; buy Oct VIX call spreads as tail hedge
bullets.body: VIX closed at 14.43, near 2025-2026 lows despite hawkish Warsh speech. VVIX re-tested lows at ~82. Institutional net VIX positioning decidedly negative (similar to pre-March spike). 22V Research recommends buying Oct 21 $22/$45 VIX call spreads for ~$1.00-$1.05 (22x max payout). September has averaged +21.85% VIX gain over past 5 years. Goldman notes options call-buying dominance with put dearth—contrarian gold hedge suggested. Private Client cash at record-low 9%.

bullets.title: NVDA RTX Spark AI PCs sell out pre-order; AMD gaining ground on agentic AI software
bullets.body: Asustek and MSI initial AI PC batches (NVDA RTX Spark, TSMC 3nm) sold out in pre-order; both requesting more chips. NVIDIA shifting unit of sale from standalone GPUs to full-stack 100MW data center systems. AMD MI455X competitive on hardware but ROCm software maturity remains key to share gains; AMD focused on AgentX benchmark. OpenAI Jalapeño chip outperforms GB300 on tokens/MW per SemiAnalysis AgentX. Vera Rubin NVL72 delivers 30x better throughput per MW vs. GB300 on agent workloads.

bullets.title: Tariff risks and USMCA breakdown create 2027 capex headwinds; tariff pass-through largely complete
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags Section 338 tariffs expose ~$20B Canadian exports to 50% duties with dollar-for-dollar Canadian retaliation; USMCA negotiations broke down in July. Trade policy uncertainty could delay non-AI and AI capex recovery in the US. Treasury Secretary Bessent plans to ask G20 to review trade terms with China over $1.2T trade surplus. Effective US tariff rate elevated but below statutory peak; pass-through to inflation largely complete. Trump also urging Canadian firms to relocate to US with tariff exemptions as incentive.
